newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips end higher on token volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips end higher on token volume.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks recouped early losses and closed firm on short-covering, dealers said.
But the broad market's decline and puny trading volume denoted underlying weakness on the bolsa.
"Prices rose a bit on short-covering although everyone is worried about next week, when we get a big batch of U.S. economic indicators," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.8 percent to 715.48, stretching the week's gains to 1.7 percent, while the broad market shed 0.2 percent.

"The market was excited by the (Standard & Poor) corporate credit rating upgrades, but now it's tuned back into U.S. interest rate worries," another broker said. "The whole point is predicting what the Federal Reserve will do with interest rates when it meets May 20."

Floor volume dwindled to 12.7 million pesos from 21 million Thursday and 29 million each in the previous two sessions, while over-the-counter turnover shrank to 79.5 million pesos from 110.9 million Thursday.
Winning issues edged out losers 19 to 16 and 23 stocks closed flat.
Best main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Sevel and steelmaker Siderar, which advanced 6.9 percent, 2.2 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by Telecom and Telefonica, off 2.0 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively, Irsa, which shed 1.4 percent, and Siderca, down 0.7 percent.
